neighbours.label: Contrast/concession discourse connectives ('but', 'however', 'even so', 'in addition', Korean -지만) at the point where a qualifying or opposing clause is about to begin; broad and weak elsewhere
fire: The first results looked promising for the new irrigation scheme, but the farmers along the lower canal saw almost no change in their yields.
She trained for months and finished the marathon in a respectable time. Even so, she told reporters she felt the race had gone badly.
The old bridge is cheap to maintain, however, and the council has no plans to replace it before the end of the decade.
Critics praised the novel's ambitious structure, yet the middle chapters were slow, and many readers admitted they skimmed them.
그들은 그 영화의 연출은 인정하지만, 결말이 너무 급하다고 느꼈다.
The committee approved the budget in March. In addition, it agreed to fund two new regional offices for the coming year.
I like most of the changes in the update, although the new menu layout takes some getting used to.
Most of the tenants paid on time; the landlord, though, insisted that the repairs could wait until spring.
quiet: The first results looked promising for the new irrigation scheme, and the farmers along the lower canal reported larger yields by autumn.
She trained for months and finished the marathon in a respectable time. She told reporters she felt the race had gone very well.
The old bridge is cheap to maintain, and the council plans to keep it open for pedestrians for many more years.
Critics praised the novel's ambitious structure, and the middle chapters drew special attention from reviewers and readers alike.
그들은 그 영화의 연출에 감탄했고 결말도 만족스러웠다고 말했다.
The committee approved the budget in March. It then met with the regional directors to discuss hiring for the coming year.
I use the update every morning because the new menu layout puts the main tools right on the front screen.
Most of the tenants paid on time; the landlord thanked each of them in a short note posted by the mailboxes.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations are mostly discourse connectives (but x5, however, in addition, even so, of course, 'Why,' and Korean 만 in -지만) in expository text, but the pole is broad (3% of tokens above 0.1 max) with a mix of other tokens (due, of, that, see, just, without), so coverage is likely partial. The census food/domain result looks like a frame artifact and I did not build the label on it.
